claims.exact_statement: There exist two binary-offspring branching models with the same per-daughter fate probabilities P(S)=p and the same mean number 2p of S daughters, but different clonal extinction probabilities. Specifically, for p>1/2, common-fate sisters give q=(1-p)/p and independent sisters give q=((1-p)/p)^2.
assumptions: Each S cell divides into exactly two daughters.
F is terminal and contributes no S offspring.
Successive parent-cell offspring vectors are iid within each named model (Galton-Watson assumption).
p is fixed, with p>1/2 for the displayed nontrivial extinction roots.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_model_counterexample; standard Galton-Watson fixed-point mechanism; no novelty or external proof claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The two generating functions and fixed-point equations are elementary standard branching-process reasoning. The counterexample is scoped; it does not claim the underlying theory is new. CLiNC already models the joint daughter-state distribution.
claims.costs: No data or computation required for the exact calculation. Biological inference would require sister-resolved lineage acquisition, clone tracking, and validation.
claims.falsifier: The mathematical statement is falsified only by an algebraic error or violation of stated offspring laws; biological relevance is falsified for a proposed assay if the observed offspring laws are effectively independent and transition-only predictions remain calibrated on held-out clones.
claims.next_gate: Acquire sister-resolved data under a regeneration/depletion intervention and compare transition-only versus joint-offspring models on held-out organoids.

claims.exact_statement: If at most H at-risk parent divisions occur, at most b daughters are produced per division, and each daughter has conditional unsafe-fate probability at most epsilon, then without any independence assumption the probability of any unsafe daughter is at most min(1,H*b*epsilon). For one b=2 division with identical marginal unsafe probability epsilon, the probability at least one daughter is unsafe lies sharply in [epsilon,min(1,2*epsilon)].
assumptions: H is a deterministic upper bound on at-risk parent divisions over the horizon.
The conditional per-daughter unsafe probability bound epsilon holds under the intervention and all relevant safe histories.
Each parent produces at most b daughters.
State classifications and lineage observations are valid.
claims.status: internally derived finite-horizon union-bound certificate; conservative; not a biological guarantee
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard union bound and Fréchet bounds; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Must acquire a defensible division-count cap H and a one-sided upper confidence bound for epsilon; imaging, barcoding, fate classification, and clone/organoid-level replication are charged.
claims.falsifier: Any intervention-matched conditional per-daughter rate above epsilon or any lineage horizon exceeding H invalidates the certificate premises.
claims.next_gate: Pre-register eta and estimate H and epsilon_U from sister-resolved perturbation data; otherwise retain UNKNOWN.

claims.exact_statement: The published human cerebral-organoid assay provides a relevant experimental interface for testing lineage-aware regeneration models: barcodes identify broad clone-size heterogeneity, and puromycin depletion of WT cells can be compensated by a minority of resistant cells under reported conditions.
assumptions: This is a source-reported result in the named in-vitro organoid setting.
The result is not generalized to in-vivo regeneration or human treatment.
claims.status: externally reported primary biological result; not independently reproduced in this lane
claims.novelty_boundary: Existing primary study; used as assay context only.
claims.costs: The proposed extension requires barcoding, organoid differentiation replicates, live paired-daughter imaging or assay, single-cell fate classification, and held-out evaluation.
claims.falsifier: The cited study's assay is not a falsifier; the proposed model relevance fails if joint offspring law does not improve held-out predictions beyond a calibrated transition-only model.
claims.next_gate: Run the preregistered paired-sister assay under vehicle and depletion/rescue conditions.
